subject.title: feat: add linux/riscv64 Docker image to multi-platform build

question: Should OpenClaw publish a best-effort standalone `:<version>-riscv64` Docker tag built through the linked separate RISC-V image path, while keeping default manifests and their current attestation boundary amd64/arm64-only?
rationale: The implementation is active and has reported runtime evidence, but selecting the supported release artifact, its provenance expectations, and its failure semantics is a maintainer product and supply-chain decision rather than a mechanical issue repair.

options.title: Sponsor the standalone tag boundary
options.body: Review the active PR as an additive best-effort RISC-V artifact that does not alter existing default manifests or their attestation workflow.

options.title: Require a fully attested multi-arch design
options.body: Pause the current PR until RISC-V can meet the same manifest and provenance contract as supported default image platforms.

options.title: Decline official RISC-V publication
options.body: Close the direction after documenting that official Docker release support remains limited to existing architectures.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the standalone tag boundary
recommendation.body: Review the active PR as an additive best-effort RISC-V artifact that does not alter existing default manifests or their attestation workflow.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Docker release, image-runtime, and attestation work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the release-boundary decision.
